text:
sam: Quick follow-up from the offload RFC — we've still got flaky races around eviction ownership handoff during compaction. Can we land on a simpler contract?

jia: +1. The current two-phase handoff leaks complexity. Seen at least two double-free-ish repros when demote and compactor overlap.

omar: Can you paste a short timeline of the race you saw? makes it easier to discuss fixes.

sam: Timeline I hit locally: 
1) tenant pins page P (owner=poolA)
2) poolA decides to demote -> sets handoff_pending = true
3) compactor sees handoff_pending, moves page to host-staging, sets owner=poolB
4) poolA finishes its work and clears pin/flags believing it still owns P -> possible double-free or lost reference.

The root is that ownership transitions aren't atomic and we have no robust precondition check.

sam: sketch of a minimal API we discussed:
```
struct EvictHandOff {
  owner_id: string;        // canonical owner performing the handoff
  page_id: u64;
  precondition_version: u64; // version that owner expects on the page meta
  ack_required: bool;
}
```

lina: What about versioned CAS on the owner field (owner, version) so compactor does CAS(old_owner, old_version -> new_owner, new_version)? That makes transition atomic.

sam: We discussed CAS. Pros: simple semantics. Cons: extra CAS on hot path (hot pages, many small batches). Need to quantify perf hit.

patrick: Alternative: keep owner canonical, but introduce a transient "handoff token". Owner issues token (signed blob with pre_version+lease). Compactor must present token to assume ownership. Token hides the two-phase from readers.

jia: Token approach looks promising. How do we handle failure mid-handshake? token TTL + explicit reclaim?

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rolled out evictor v2 to staging (rev 5f3a) :rocket:

omar: If token has TTL, you need a reclaim path: original owner can reclaim when token expired if pinned==0, otherwise extend token. Also need to avoid token flooding in GC storms.

sam: Proposed minimal rules: single-writer rule — only current owner can mint a handoff_token. Token includes pre_version and lease_ms. Compactor validates token then attempts CAS(owner, pre_version -> new_owner, pre_version+1). If CAS fails, compactor aborts and cleans up token. If token expires, owner may reclaim or reissue.

lina: Nice. For safety we should add a small probation window where both owners treat page as read-only until ack. Avoids races with in-flight pins.

sam: Agreed. Next steps: I'll draft an RFC addendum describing the token contract, the CAS fallback, and a microbench plan (simulate 100k ops/s with 1% handoff rate to measure CAS latency/failure). Ping me if you want to help with sim harness.

patrick: I'm in for the bench. Also +1 on a small probation period to reduce rare races.

jia: Thanks — this should simplify the allocator surface and reduce sporadic compactor bugs.

sam: Cool — will post the addendum later today.
